title: CHARGE-RIVER: buried-channel oxide CCD strings, scheduled like a drum for LLM weight and KV streaming
status_reason: No physics kill, but the step-change claim shrinks. (1) The original two-ended regeneration had no return path; the fix needs a speculative deck-joint regenerator tier, or a 2x tighter CTE (0.9987 vs 0.9973) in a one-way 64-stage string. (2) Staircases cost ~29% of array area. (3) Realistic $25/plate plus the new tiers erase the cost advantage: $1.74/GB, 0.85x DDR5. Density falls from 3.6x to ~2.5x 1-beta and the cost leg is killed. The buried-channel factor weakens (0.18 -> 0.28) and RTN must be screened. P(pass) is lower and still hinges on imec's unread CTE definition.

revised_verdicts.possible: YES (revised after red team): no law is violated and no physics kill was found, but three specs tightened. The buried heterochannel needs dEc >=0.5 eV at 4.5e12 cm-2 (0.3 eV leaves ~1.4 kT). Oxide-SF RTN must be screened at the 2-5 ns CDS timescale. Each segment must be injected at one end and sensed at the other.
revised_verdicts.profitable: STEP CHANGE IF IT WORKS: DENSITY ~2.5x 1-beta (1.14 Gb/mm2; 2.2-2.7x over strip lengths; ~3.5x only with speculative staircase-free contacts), plus ~158x lower refresh/standby power and ~2.4-3x lower energy per useful bit than HBM3 including I/O, for a scheduled LLM streaming tier. Cost per bit is ~parity ($1.74/GB, 0.85x; 0.7-1.5x range), no longer a step change. Was 3.6x density and 2.1x cost.
revised_verdicts.doable: PARTLY: $994k over 24 months can prove or kill the device physics: CTE >=0.9973 at 150 MT/s on an overlapping-gate reference, buried >=3x vs surface, RTN tails on >=1e4 nodes at real CDS timing, a regenerated 98-transfer loop at BER <=5e-10 and a 12-plate vertical coupon. It cannot prove AR-40 conformal heterostack decks, the deck-joint regenerator tier, the staircase or cost; those are $10-50M partner milestones.

revised_experiment: Steps: (1) M0: read imec's IEDM 2024 / IMW 2026 papers and restate P; a $20k professional FTO. (2) M0-2: Poisson-Schrodinger (full-fill packet >=2 nm from interfaces) and vertical-gap electrostatics; XPS band offsets at Argonne (target dEc >=0.5 eV, cap <=2.5 nm). (3) Run 1, planar 3-phase CCDs: overlapping two-level gates as the GATE-scoring reference plus single-level 12-20 nm gap proxies; surface, buried and Ga-free channels at matched 4.5e12 cm-2; +-10% composition corners; W-fill-chemistry exposure splits. Alongside: ALD composition vs depth in AR 40-80 test structures (TEM/EDX), and an RTN node array of >=1e4 oxide FD-SF cells sampled at the real 2-5 ns CDS interval (>=1e7 samples per node). (4) GATE 1 (M10): median CTE >=0.9973 with DFE at >=150 MT/s, 25 and 85 C, and buried deferral >=3x below surface. (5) RTN gate (M12-16): 1e-9 per-read step quantile <=30 e- after sparing <=2%. (6) M14-20: a 12-plate vertical buried-channel coupon at >=50 MHz. (7) DEMO (M18-21): an inject-bottom/sense-top 98-transfer loop through an FPGA/sky130 regenerator, >=1e12 decisions at a 50 MHz stage clock, 25 and 85 C, raw BER <=5e-10; plus a 194-transfer one-way loop for the fallback. (8) Trace simulator: >=92% of bytes with >=0.64 us lead; energy per useful bit incl. I/O. Cost: $994k fully loaded ($519k direct), 24 months.

responses.response: Valid for the original two-ended design, which needed FD+RST+SF+SEL plus a fill-and-spill injector at each end (~10-14 TFTs per hole), none of it priced. Redesign: (1) Injection needs no per-hole TFT. It uses fill-and-spill (potential equilibration) from a per-column injection line, and the hole is selected by its strip's input-gate plate. The packet is set by the input-gate barrier and the well capacitance, not by the line. (2) Sensing happens only at segment tops. The FD is shared by 2 holes on one column line from adjacent strips, which are never read together. That gives one RST/SF/SEL set per 2 holes, i.e. 1.5 TFT per hole per sensing level, in a 0.054 um2 footprint (2 holes including slit share) against PIXEL-STACK's 0.034 um2 per set: one sub-layer with 1.6x margin. (3) This is the I-12302 principle: clamp the long column line and sense a short local strip with a gain FET. Dumping 313 e- onto a ~51 fF column would give ~1 mV, against 125 mV on a 0.40 fF strip (Micron planar plate-sensing patents narrow any claim). Priced in the model: array base $1,200 -> $1,500 for the top tier and bottom lines, +$500 for the joint tier (CIRC-02), C_FD 0.30 -> 0.40 fF, read noise 8 -> 10 e-. The floor moves 0.9970 -> 0.9973. The TFTs fit the footprint, so density is not reduced; their cost is inside the revised $1.74/GB.
responses.action: Model inputs revised (array_base_usd, c_fd_fF, sigma_read_e, joint_tier_usd). Add a shared-FD layout and a >=1e4-node FD-SF array to runs 1-2. State 1.5 TFT per hole per sensing level, and 0 at injection ends, in the dossier.

responses.response: Correct, and the most consequential circuit objection: the original 'sense and re-inject at each end' scheme has no physical return path. Modeled options (model section 4c): (a) LIFO bidirectional at each end: the worst bit sees 194 transfers; it needs a bottom sense node and a 32-bit buffer per node (~32 Mb, 5-8 mm2) and doubles plate cycles to 3e11. Rejected. (b) One-way 64-stage string, injected at the bottom and sensed at the top, decisions returned through the CMOS: 64 b/hole with no new tier, but 194 transfers raise the CTE floor 0.9973 -> 0.9987 (2x less deferral allowed). The lap becomes 1.28 us (s >= 96.1%; MoE + sparse attention averages 58 ns) and cycles 3e11; 1.18 Gb/mm2, $1.58/GB. (c) 'Joint': two 100-plate decks with an oxide-TFT regenerator tier at the deck joint. The lower deck is sensed at the joint and the upper deck injected there. It keeps 2 x 32 stages, 98 transfers, the ~0.997 floor, a 0.64 us lap and 1.5e11 cycles, at +$500/wafer and 4% TAV area. Bonus: ALD at AR 40 per deck and no CCD transfer across the deck joint. But no one has built a TFT tier between stack decks [SPECULATIVE]. A P-BiCS U-string doubles the loop per regenerator (128 stages at 200 plates), so it is worse. Base = (c), fallback = (b).
responses.action: Downgrade: 64 b/hole at ~0.997 now depends on a speculative deck-joint tier, and without it the GO line is CTE >= 0.9987 (the old STRONG-GO). The seed loop demo implements inject-at-one-end / sense-at-other with an FPGA/sky130 return path, and also runs a 194-transfer one-way loop to price the fallback. The joint tier is a $10-50M partner milestone.

responses.response: Accepted. The like-for-like model adds an HBM-class 1.0 pJ/bit I/O term and cuts clock recovery from 50% to 33%: 3-phase charge sharing or 3-step stepwise charging, since on-chip LC would need uH inductors. Streaming then costs 1.09 pJ/bit including I/O. A random 64 B access laps a whole clock strip (150 um x 2 rows = 2,121 holes) for 512 useful bits: 15.9 pJ per useful bit plus I/O, worse than a DRAM row activation. CIRC's per-hole ~1.4 pJ is if anything optimistic. Weighted by the 0.5-2% random floor this gives 1.17-1.40 pJ per useful bit, ~2.4-2.9x below HBM3's 3.44 pJ, not the ~48x a core-versus-total comparison implied. The scrub-versus-refresh saving falls from 191x to ~158x with the lower recovery.
responses.action: Energy claim restated as ~2.4-3x per useful bit including I/O, with the refresh/standby step at ~158x. The simulator reports energy per useful bit on measured trace mixes. The sky130 chip carries a 3-step stepwise clock-driver test.

responses.response: Accepted and modeled (model section 4b). The eye at the floor is 191 e- wide (half-width ~95 e-). RTN model: exponential steps with eta 1.4/2.8/4.2 mV (3.5/7.0/10.5 e- at 401 uV/e-); 20% of nodes have a fast trap, which switches between CDS samples with probability 0.25. Unscreened floors are 0.9975 / 0.9993 / fails at any CTE. Screening out nodes with a measured step >25 e- spares 0% / 0.56% / 1.8% of nodes and returns the floor to 0.9975-0.9976. With 2-hole FD sharing a spare costs 2 holes x 32 b, not 512 holes x 64 b, and the overhead is carried in spare_frac 0.03 (2% strings + 1% nodes), which costs 3% of density. Insurance against traps activating after the screen, from the I-12627 principle: two independent SFs per FD, averaged, with a disagreement flag that re-samples the still-held FD. The per-read event probability falls 5e-2 -> ~3e-3 and the amplitude tail enters squared, if trap sites are independent.
responses.action: Add an RTN node array: >=1e4 oxide FD-SF cells with on-die oxide sample-and-hold at the real 2-5 ns CDS interval, >=1e7 samples per node ($15k). New GO line: 1e-9 per-read step quantile <=30 e- after sparing <=2% of nodes. In-field re-screen during scrub. Sparing included in density.

responses.response: Largely right at the dossier's stated spec. Electrostatics (model section 5a) at 4.5e12 cm-2: E_F sits 36 meV above the subband, 170 mV drops across a 2.5 nm cap (eps 12) and E0 is ~50 meV. That leaves a margin of 44 meV, i.e. 1.4 kT at 85 C (0.3 kT with a 3 nm cap), so the top of each '1' packet reaches the cap/dielectric interface, and +-0.05 eV composition swings move the estimated interface-loss removal between ~0.3 and ~0.9. Not fatal, because heterostructures hold far more sheet charge than doping-defined Si BCCDs once the offset is larger. At dEc 0.5 eV with a <=2.5 nm cap the margin is ~7.9 kT; at 0.4 eV it is 4.7 kT. Reported offsets: IGZO/beta-Ga2O3 0.71+-0.1 eV (XPS), high-In IGZO/IGZO ~0.4 eV, but In2O3/Ga2O3 only 0.09 eV. They are method- and composition-dependent, and Ga-rich caps conflict with the Ga-free aim. Model: eta_buried 0.9 -> 0.5, so the buried + fat-zero deferral factor goes 0.18 -> 0.28 until measured. The per-transfer reading of imec stays NO-GO (buried, 25 C: 0.88-0.99); the end-to-end reading stays GO (~75x margin).
responses.action: Raise the offset spec from >=0.3 to >=0.5 eV with a <=2.5 nm cap. Solve Poisson-Schrodinger at full fill by M2, with DEV's criterion that the charge sits >=2 nm from any interface. Measure XPS band offsets at Argonne on every stack before run 1. GATE 1 keeps 'buried >=3x lower deferral than surface at matched 4.5e12 cm-2, 50 MHz, 25 C', now scored on the overlapping-gate reference. Fallback: 2.5e12 cm-2 (173 e- packets) holds >=4 kT even at 0.3 eV but needs CTE ~0.999.

responses.response: Same physics as CIRC-04; accepted. With the revised 0.40 fF FD, eta 1.4-4.2 mV is 3.5-10.5 e-. With p_fast 0.2 and p_switch 0.25, the unscreened 1e-9 per-read step quantile is 62/124/186 e- against a ~95 e- eye half-width. So 2.8 mV moves the floor to 0.9993 and 4.2 mV fails at any CTE: a Gaussian 8 e- term does hide this. Mitigation without halving density: (1) screen and spare at 25 e- (<=1.8% of nodes at 4.2 mV; floor back to 0.9976); (2) a larger SF gate (eta scales as 1/WL, so a 100 x 200 nm gate halves it, fits the 2-hole footprint and, being bootstrapped, barely raises C_FD); (3) in-field re-screen during scrub; (4) the I-12627 dual-SF option. Silicon sensing at both ends is no longer needed, because the bottom and joint ends are injection-only in the new topology.
responses.action: Adopt DEV's test as a GO criterion: measured 1e-9 per-read between-sample step quantile <=30 e- on >=1e4 oxide FD-SF nodes at the 2-5 ns CDS interval, after sparing <=2%. New kill: >5% of nodes must be spared to reach 30 e-. Revival: bonded Si SF at >=1 um pitch with 8-hole FD sharing, or >=600 e- packets.

responses.response: Valid, and planar coupons cannot prove it. What changes: (1) The joint topology splits the stack into two 100-plate decks, each with its own ALD channel at AR 40, and removes any CCD transfer across the deck joint, because the joint is a sense/inject interface. That eliminates the joint step or pocket. (2) Robustness: at dEc >=0.5 eV a +-0.05 eV swing leaves >=6 kT of margin. Smooth top-to-bottom grading (50 mV over 100 plates = 0.5 meV per plate) is common to all strings and absorbed by per-depth DFE kernels and clock trims. Fat zero neutralises static pockets below 47 e-. An abrupt 30 mV (~1 kT) step is inside the ~2.5-3 kT barrier tolerance at a 6.7 ns dwell (model section 5b). (3) In-seed evidence: multi-cation ALD composition versus depth in AR 40-80 conformality test structures with TEM/EDX; planar composition-corner CCDs (+-10% In/Ga) to measure dCTE/dcomposition; and a 12-plate vertical coupon at low AR. CTE of a full AR-40 deck remains a partner milestone.
responses.action: Provability downgrade: the vertical leg can be bounded but not proven in the seed, so 'PROVABLE WITH $1M' falls to PARTLY. Add LHAR TEM/EDX, composition corners and the 12-plate coupon (~$80k). New kill: a top-to-bottom composition spread >10% that the corners show moves CTE by >5e-4.

responses.response: Accepted that the model lacked a gap term; it now has one (model section 5b). Barrier: escape time tau_b = tau_diff(40 nm) x exp(dV/kT). Charge stranded after a 6.67 ns dwell stays below 20% of the deferral budget (3.6e-4) up to ~2.5-3 kT (65-90 mV), so DEV's <0.5 kT criterion is stricter than the transport needs. Pocket: a static pocket smaller than the fat zero (47 e-) stays permanently filled and causes no data-dependent loss. With ~0.014 fF of gap coupling that covers pockets several hundred mV deep. The residual risk is signal-dependent pockets. Evidence: MIT LL's fast single-poly Si CCDs work with narrow gaps, and the vertical gap is a deposited oxide film, more uniform than an e-beam gap.
responses.action: By M2, 2D/3D electrostatics of the curved vertical gap at full and fat-zero fill (pass: barrier <=2 kT, signal-dependent pocket <=5 e-). Planar CTE against gap width 12-20 nm. The 12-plate vertical coupon measures the real deposited gap.

responses.response: Accepted. k_ws is redefined from a natural tail to a screen threshold. Every string's deferral is measured at test and re-measured each scrub (per-string DFE kernels are extracted anyway), and strings above 1.5x median are mapped out, as NAND bad blocks are. Spare cost = P(bulk lognormal > 1.5x) + rare-defect share. For bulk sigma_ln 0.10 / 0.15 / 0.20 (Poisson spread of 1e2-1e3 traps plus CD spread) that is 0.003% / 0.34% / 2.1%, plus ~0.1-1% rare defects. It is carried as 2% strings inside spare_frac 0.03. If sigma_ln reaches 0.3, spares at 1.5x would be 8.8%; then run k_ws 2 (1.0% spared, floor 0.9973 -> 0.9980). The 1e-8 tail is a yield/sparing number measurable only on Gb-class arrays.
responses.action: String-screen and spare-map architecture added; spare overhead included in density. The seed measures the bulk distribution to the 1e-3-1e-4 quantile on narrow channels and the vertical coupon. A defect-model extrapolation to 1e-8 is a raise-stage deliverable.

responses.response: Accepted as a defensibility downgrade, not a physics one. imec has planar (2024) and vertical (2026) oxide CCDs, and our original claims are narrowed on every side. Changes: (1) a professional FTO/patentability search of imec and SEL oxide-CCD filings 2022-26, budgeted at $20k (was $3-5k) and done before any provisional; (2) claims refocused on what the red team forced and imec has not published: the channel-last replacement-gate oxide CCD flow, inject-bottom/sense-top regeneration with a deck-joint regenerator tier, RTN-screened shared-FD readout with per-string deferral screening and sparing, a >=0.5 eV buried heterochannel at >=4e12 cm-2, and the lead-time placement controller; (3) a cross-licence needs a measured advantage imec lacks, i.e. buried deferral >=3x below surface at 150 MT/s. MISSION excludes business kills, so this lowers defensibility, not physical possibility.
responses.action: FTO by M2. GATE 1's buried >=3x result is the IP-bearing measurement. If FTO shows imec claims the buried heterochannel, drop claim #1 and file on the readout, regeneration and integration claims.

responses.response: Accepted, and worse than stated. With all red-team corrections ($25/plate, 29% staircase, spares, joint tier, 100 nm slits) cost is $1.74/GB for the joint base (0.85x DDR5) and $1.58/GB one-way (0.93x); even at yield 0.95 it is $1.46/GB. The cost leg is withdrawn (PROC-04). What remains: density ~2.5x 1-beta per mm2 (capacity per die and stack), ~158x lower refresh/standby power and ~2.4-3x lower energy per useful bit than HBM3, at scheduled DRAM-class latency and high endurance. Against HBF it is positioned as the write-endurant KV-cache tier: NAND tolerates ~1e3-1e5 writes per cell [training knowledge], while KV cache is rewritten every token. yield_rel 0.8 stays as a mature-stage guess with 0.5-0.95 carried, and the parity conclusion holds across that range. The Optane analogy is a business risk, which MISSION excludes from kills.
responses.action: Restate the step change as density plus standby/refresh energy, not cost. In Q4, hold buyer-discovery talks (accelerator vendor, hyperscaler) for a write-endurant streaming-tier price/latency spec (no budget). Getting that spec is a raise-stage gate.

responses.response: Accepted. A search this session confirmed the record: IEDM 2024 paper 37-6, R. Kishore et al., DOI 10.1109/iedm50854.2024.10873539. The public abstract still says only 'CTE >98%' (plus 'multilevel capability'), so the definition is still unknown. P is therefore restated conditionally, not as a point: P(GATE 1 pass) ~10-20% if imec's 98% is per transfer (lower than the earlier 15-25%, because the buried factor is now 0.28 and the floor rose to 0.9973), and ~40-50% if end-to-end (~75x CTE margin on the trap-kinetics carry-over, but the buried >=3x condition is now harder). Until the paper is read, this dossier's P should not break the EV tie with LEAN ARRAY MODULE in either direction.
responses.action: Buy and read the IEDM 2024 and IMW 2026 papers in week 1 (M0), before any spending, and restate P. If the 98% is per transfer and imec shows <2x from a buried channel or fat zero, apply kill criterion 1.

responses.response: Partly accepted. Planar CCDs at 150 MT/s and matched sheet charge are necessary, because they measure the channel physics, but they are not enough to look ahead of imec. Change: the seed now also builds a 12-plate vertical CCD coupon: 4 three-phase stages; a W or Mo/SiO2 stack of ~0.5-0.7 um; ~250 nm holes at AR ~3; e-beam multi-depth contacts instead of a staircase; the buried heterochannel and a bottom injection contact. It targets >=50 MHz. A vertical, buried-channel result at ~10x imec's >4 MHz would lead on clock and channel. AR-40/80 decks remain partner work (MIT LL, Albany NY CREATES, imec). 'Why a company' is a business question that MISSION does not kill on. The honest answer is that the company's asset is channel, readout and integration know-how plus IP, most likely monetised through memory-maker partners.
responses.action: Vertical coupon at M14-20 ($50k plus shared fab hours, funded by merging run 2 and cutting contingency). Partner outreach after FTO and provisionals.

responses.response: Accepted for the gate-first spec. 5 um of blanket W at ~1 GPa bows a 300 mm wafer ~3 mm (Stoney: 3 x 1e9 x 5e-6 x 0.15^2 / (180e9 x 775e-6^2)), and a 60 nm slit through 8 um of metal is AR ~130. Redesign: adopt NAND's ONON stack with replacement W and slits >=100 nm, inheriting NAND's bow management (slit-segmented W, low-stress W, backside compensation, decks). Use a channel-LAST order: gate/blocking dielectric liner in the hole, sacrificial core, W replacement through the slits, an outgas anneal, then core removal and the ALD oxide channel at <=400 C. WF6/H2 then never touches the channel. Slit efficiency stays at 0.74 by moving to 2-row strips with half-pitch column lines (was 0.70 with 1-row strips and 60 nm slits). Two 100-plate decks halve each etch to AR 40.
responses.action: In run 1, expose planar coupons to the W-fill chemistry and thermal cycle, and split channel-last against channel-first (pass: dCTE <5e-4, PROC's criterion). Bow and slit etch on a real stack are partner milestones on a NAND tool set.

responses.response: Accepted; the dossier's 'no staircase, 3-6 clock contacts' was wrong. Every buried plate needs a contact step at each driven strip end. Strip length is RC-limited to ~100-200 um at 50 MHz, and RC per um2 does not depend on strip width, so wider strips do not help. At 0.3 um per step and 150 um strips, the 200-plate staircase costs 29% of array area (efficiency 0.71; 0.62-0.77 over 100-200 um), inside PROC's 23-38% band. With the other corrections, density falls 1.62 -> 1.14 Gb/mm2 (3.6x -> 2.5x; 2.2-2.7x over strip lengths). Per-row clocking is kept: 2-row strips with half-pitch column lines read both rows at once, so cycles are not multiplied. A [SPECULATIVE] staircase-free scheme, with three sacrificial plate materials and each phase contacted through its own trench after selectively recessing the other two (~3 um per end), would restore 0.98 efficiency (1.56 Gb/mm2, 3.5x). No such process exists.
responses.action: Downgrade: density -29% from the staircase alone. Staircase now in the model. The staircase-free phase contact is listed as a $10-50M-stage process development and IP candidate. A plate-contact layout with RC <=2 ns is a partner milestone.

responses.response: Accepted for the original two-ended design: a bottom node shared by 8-16 holes has C_FD 1-2 fF and 25-50 e- of noise. The redesign removes the bottom sense node. In both new topologies the hole bottom only injects, by fill-and-spill (potential equilibration) from a per-column line, and the packet does not depend on the line's capacitance. Low-noise FDs exist only at segment tops (the hole top, plus the deck joint in the joint topology), where a TFT tier can be patterned. There the FD is shared by 2 holes at ~0.40 fF, giving 10 e- of read noise. The hole bottom still needs a NAND-like bottom punch or backside exposure, plus per-column bottom lines at 70 nm pitch. Landing a deep hole on a line is an overlay risk, eased by AR-40 decks. CMOS goes under the array, or bonds only at subarray edges, never at hole pitch.
responses.action: Model: C_FD 0.30 -> 0.40 fF, read noise 8 -> 10 e-. The vertical coupon includes a bottom injection contact. GATE 2 item: measured read noise <=10 e- on the coupon's top FD.

responses.response: Accepted. Searches this session found TechInsights' view that going from 64 to 96 layers cut cost only ~10-15%, and that 3D NAND bit cost follows ~0.7x per node and levels out at 300-400 layers. Neither gives a direct 200-layer per-layer cost. A metal/oxide pair (or ONON plus replacement W) carrying its share of HAR hole etch, slit etch, staircase litho-trim cycles and W fill plausibly costs what a NAND layer costs: base $25 (range $12-35). Model: the wafer goes $5,280 -> $9,050. That gives $1.74/GB (0.85x DDR5) for the joint base and $1.58 (0.93x) one-way. At $15/plate it is 1.09-1.22x. >=1.5x needs <=~$15/plate AND staircase-free contacts ($12: $0.91/GB, 1.63x). The cost-per-bit step change does not survive.
responses.action: Kills the cost-per-bit leg; the concept survives on density and standby energy. Revival condition: a NAND-maker or reverse-costing figure <=$12 per plate pair AND staircase-free phase contacts (>=1.6x). A $5k reverse-costing check is in the budget.

responses.response: Accepted. Run 1 adds overlapping two-level gates (W / ALD Al2O3 inter-gate dielectric / W, a standard university-fab build) as the process-clean physics reference. GATE 1 PASS/FAIL, including buried versus surface at matched charge, is scored on those structures. The single-level 12-20 nm e-beam-gap structures are scored separately as the vertical-geometry proxy (CTE versus gap width), so a NO-GO now requires failure on the overlapping-gate reference. Precedent: MIT LL's fast single-poly CCDs show single-level gates work when gaps are narrow and controlled. The vertical gap is a deposited film, more uniform than an e-beam gap.
responses.action: +1 mask and ALD level in run 1 (inside the revised $50k materials and $35k e-beam lines). GATE 1 rule rewritten. Ask MIT LL or imec for reference structures to cross-calibrate.

responses.response: Accepted that planar coupons cannot measure it. Two distinctions reduce its bite. First, smooth top-to-bottom grading is common to every string at a given depth: it shifts the median, which per-depth DFE kernels and clock trims absorb, rather than adding to k_ws, which is string-to-string. Second, at dEc >=0.5 eV a +-10% composition swing (~+-0.05 eV) still leaves >=6 kT of buried margin. Abrupt local variation does feed k_ws, and that is screened and spared (DEV-05). In-seed measurements: TEM-EDX composition at the top, middle and bottom of AR 40-80 conformality test structures coated with our multi-cation ALD supercycle (PROC's +-10% criterion), plus planar composition-corner CCDs (+-10% In/Ga) to measure CTE and offset sensitivity. Together they turn the measured grading into a predicted vertical k_ws contribution. The joint topology halves the per-deck AR to 40.
responses.action: ~$30k for LHAR test chips, TEM/EDX and corner splits. GATE 2 adds: composition within +-10% top-to-bottom at AR >=40, and predicted k_ws <=1.5.
